rows.first_problematic_claim: In every case g^2 is not congruent to 1 modulo p^2; hence v_p(g^2-1)=1.
rows.failed_obligation: For p>3, a primitive root modulo p is not congruent to plus or minus 1 modulo p, so p does not divide g^2-1 and v_p(g^2-1)=0, not 1. The stated valuation holds only in the p=3 case.
rows.minimal_repair_direction: Split p=3 from p>3 and recompute the valuation; this ordering does not yield the required nondivisibility by p^n for p>3, so give a different permutation or construction there.
rows.reason: Cyclicity and the primitive-root lifting fact used earlier are standard algebraic facts, and n19 follows from primitivity modulo p^n for n>=2. Node n25 is the first false inference.

rows.first_problematic_claim: n^2+n+t divides (n+t)^2 is equivalent to n^2+n+t divides t^2+2nt.
rows.failed_obligation: Subtracting n^2+n+t from (n+t)^2 leaves t^2+2nt-n-t, not t^2+2nt. Thus the stated divisibility equivalence is generally false.
rows.minimal_repair_direction: Use the correct remainder t^2+2nt-n-t, then derive and justify the quotient/Pell-equation classification from that corrected condition.
